root_cause.text: ext4_mb_release() only drained queued discard work when the current mount option had DISCARD set, but if the filesystem was remounted with nodiscard after previously having discard enabled, pending s_discard_work would not be flushed on unmount, potentially causing use-after-free or other memory corruption.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states: "If the filesystem is initially mounted with the discard option, deleting files will populate sbi->s_discard_list and queue s_discard_work. If it is then remounted with nodiscard, the EXT4_MOUNT_DISCARD flag is cleared, but the pending s_discard_work is neither cancelled nor flushed." The patch removes the conditional `if (test_opt(sb, DISCARD))` around `flush_work(&sbi->s_discard_work);` and `WARN_ON_ONCE(...)`, making them unconditional in `ext4_mb_release()`.
